item.title: Bears linked to former Pro Bowler in an unexpected trade move
item.description: Bears linked to former Pro Bowler in an unexpected trade move originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL's trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, and that means it's down to the wire for teams looking to make deals . After the deadline arrives, player contracts will no longer be assigned or traded from one franchise to another. Any trade deal has to be agreed to before that cutoff, which lands at 4 p.m. ET. In a feature published Thursday on ESPN , Bill Barnwell names a handful of trade ideas that could happen before the deadline hits. The Chicago Bears are one of the teams that could certainly pull off a trade. They're on the edge of the playoffs, and this is the moment to go for it. Chicago Bears could reunite with familiar Pro Bowl cornerback in bargain trade In the piece, Barnwell names a "bargain target" for Ben Johnson and the Bears. It's a familiar name and a Pro Bowler. "What about a different sort of reunion?" he asks. "Nahshon Wright was a surprise starter for the Bears a year ago owing to injuries ahead of him on the depth chart, and while the 2021 third-round pick took some risks in coverage, the good outweighed the bad." He adds, "Wright picked off five passes and earned a Pro Bowl nod before signing a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Jets ." Is Wright the answer to all of the Bears' woes? No. But he would be quite the bang for the buck, as Barnwell notes, and could provide just the little boost this team needs as the season enters its final stretch. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Dak Prescott is sure Cowboys have an identity, but it might not be a good one appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dak Prescott just dropped a candid quote hinting at how things are going on the offensive side of the ball for the Dallas Cowboys . Asked on Thursday about the identity of the Cowboys on offense, Prescott responded with an intriguing line. “Yeah sure, I mean, is it one we’re proud of? I don’t know,” the former Mississippi State Bulldogs star quarterback replied, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Cowboys have one of the most prolific offenses in the league through eight weeks of action in the 2026 NFL season. They enter Week 9 seventh in the league with 27.4 points per game. However, they are just 13th with an average of 342.0 total yards per contest. Prescott didn’t seem to reveal what exactly the identity was he was talking about, but there surely is a lot to be improved on the team’s attack. For one, the Cowboys are averaging only 94.1 rushing yards per game. Only seven teams average fewer yards on the ground this season than Dallas, but it’s also worth noting that the Cowboys are fifth with 1.25 rushing scores per outing. The Cowboys are coming off an extremely disappointing loss in Week 8 to Gardner Minshew II and the Arizona Cardinals in Arlington. Dallas wasted a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter in a 33-30 overtime defeat to the visiting Cardinals, with the Cowboys unable to score in their overtime drive. item.title: Anderson could be given chance to join Surrey
item.description: James Anderson played 188 Tests, claiming 704 wickets [Getty Images] James Anderson could be given the opportunity to extend his legendary career by joining Surrey. England's all-time leading wicket-taker has left Lancashire after not being offered a contract by the county for whom he first played professionally 25 years ago. Although he will turn 45 in July 2027, Anderson has stopped short of retiring and said on his Tailenders podcast last week: "I am starting to get excited about the future, whether it is something different or playing cricket again. It is exciting." In the days after news emerged of Anderson's exit from Lancashire, a number of clubs from both divisions of the County Championship expressed an interest in speaking to the seamer. Though neither Anderson's camp nor Surrey have commented, a move to The Oval would appear to make sense for both player and county. Surrey have the financial means to sign Anderson and his addition would help a squad that features nine players on England central contracts. Of the nine, three are frontline seamers who would be regulars around Surrey's Championship team: Gus Atkinson, Matthew Fisher and Henry Crocombe. Crocombe, a new arrival from Sussex, and Fisher have been given England deals for the first time. For Anderson, joining a county with Surrey's depth would present the opportunity for a managed workload. Playing a relatively reduced role for Surrey would perhaps avoid the need to move from his home in Cheshire. It would also provide the chance to end his remarkable career with a challenge to win the County Championship. With Surrey and Lancashire in different divisions of the Championship, it would even allow Anderson to continue playing without the prospect of coming up against his boyhood club. Lancashire consider Anderson farewell amid fan unrest Surrey director of cricket Alec Stewart was in the England team when Anderson made his debut in a one-day international against Australia in Melbourne in 2002. Anderson first played List A cricket in 2000 as a 17-year-old for the Lancashire Cricket Board against Suffolk. In addition to his 911 international wickets - an England record and a record for all pace bowlers - Anderson claimed 443 first-class scalps for Lancashire, along with 83 in List A cricket and a further 50 in T20s. Last season, he was Lancashire captain as the county struggled, eventually finishing second-bottom of Division Two. Still, Anderson's form remained strong and he collected 50 Championship wickets at an average of 17. Speaking at length on Tailenders, Anderson said he was "sad" and "shocked" to be told he was no longer required as a player at Old Trafford. "I am sad the way it ended with the club I supported as a kid, but now I have thought about it I am quite excited for the future," he said. "I am always going to support Lancashire. item.title: Alex Highsmith reveals what has helped the Steelers’ defense play at a high level
item.description: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defense held the Cleveland Browns to season lows in points and rushing yards in their dominant 27-6 victory at Acrisure Stadium this past Sunday. As they enter the bye, the Steelers defense ranks third in scoring defense, allowing just 18 points per game through eight games. However, it wasn’t always sunshine and rainbows for the defensive unit early in the season. In fact, the first time the Steelers and Browns met this season, T.J. Watt was caught yelling into a headset on the sideline at defense coordinator Patrick Graham after a miscommunication led to a Cleveland touchdown. After that game, Graham moved from the booth to the sidelines with his players. The Steelers have rattled off four consecutive wins since Graham moved to the sidelines, backed by exceptional defensive play. Appearing on “NFL Report” with Andrew Siciliano , Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith detailed how Graham’s move down to the sidelines has changed the Steelers’ defense. “You know, I do believe that was a turning point for us,” Highsmith said. “Obviously, he’s been on the field with us ever since and so just him being down there is just really helped us a lot, for sure. But, you know PG’s been awesome, ever since he came in he’s just had a desire for us to be great. He’s a football guy, he knows football so well, and so I just think as we continue to gel as a unit, gel as a defense, you know it’s only going to be better from here on out. Like I said, I just love the way we are progressing as a defense so we just gotta continue to play like we have been and with him (Graham) calling plays, just excited to see what he continues to scheme up to put guys in positions to make plays.” Steelers undefeated (4-0) since DC Patrick Graham listened to Amy Winehouse on the Ohio Turnpike. 🎥 Alex Highsmith on @NFL Report @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NAwDdbpqPw — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) November 4, 2026 Pittsburgh boasts the third most takeaways in the league with 13, while allowing just 83.9 rushing yards per game to opponents at the midway point in their season. It seems like Pittsburgh finally has the right man leading the charge defensively in Graham. Highsmith’s praise of the scheme and putting guys in positions to make plays is a great sign that the players have bought into what Graham is selling them. The Steelers look well on their way to having their first season with a top-ten scoring defense since 2023, and it seems like it only took a simple move to the sidelines to make a world of difference. Whether due to injuries or poor performance, Week 9 will feature some unlikely names taking QB1 snaps — with some of those situations being better than others. OLAF KRAAK / ANP (Photo by ANP via Getty Images) | ANP via Getty Images For the overwhelming majority of Thursday night’s trip to the Netherlands, Juventus looked like a team that, somewhat surprisingly, was in control of things. They had a 2-0 lead, their defense was looking rather solid and AZ Alkmaar was being forced to settle for low-percentage shots through traffic that ended up doing exactly as you think they might have — next to nothing. Around the 70th or 75th minute, though, things changed. And in a hurry. From that point on, what was looking like it could be a relatively calm trip across the finish line turned into anything but that. Not only did AZ Alkmaar cut Juve’s lead in half, but they nearly tied things up, only for a very close — yet also very obvious — offside call there to save the day. Juventus held on for the 2-1 victory to make finish the first half of the Europa League league phase with a win, but it was another instance of just how quickly things can change for this team when they’re either disrupted by their own mistakes, some questionable individual efforts or just about anything else you can think of that applies here. But it was a win, and Juventus will be taking three points back with them to Turin, moving one step closer to a potential finish in the top eight and not having to shoehorn two more games into the schedule for a squad that has played a ton of minutes over the last 3 1/2 weeks. That stretch is nearly over, though. That nine-game run over the span of 29 days is about to hit its last step come this weekend in Florence. After that, an international break where … there probably won’t be a lot of rest for a decent chunk of the squad that isn’t actually injured. For the others, they can get some sort of respite from the hellacious fixture list that we’ve seen this team go through between the first and second international breaks of the 2026-27 season. The thing is, after falling from the top of the Europa League table with their draw against Stade Rennes a couple of weeks ago, Juve are now back to winning in Europe. item.title: Miami gets reported bad news on Malachi Toney before Notre Dame game
item.description: Miami Hurricanes receiver Malachi Toney hurt his ankle at practice on Wednesday ahead of Saturday’s trip to the Notre Dame Fighting Irish, and by that night the concern around him had moved well past Saturday. Toney has a high ankle sprain and will have surgery, ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported , with a recovery that typically takes at least four weeks and a plan aimed at getting him back for the College Football Playoff. The Associated Press’ Tim Reynolds, citing an unnamed source, reported that the initial timeline will come after the operation. Miami’s own statement said only that Toney was undergoing further evaluation. Saturday will be the first game the Heisman Trophy candidate misses since enrolling at Miami, after he played in all 24 of the program’s games over the last two seasons. He has 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this year, which accounts for 35% of Miami’s catches, 39% of its receiving yards and 46% of its touchdown receptions. item.title: Melbourne native Lachlan Carrigan named to Ray Guy Award watch list for USC
item.description: LOS ANGELES — USC punter Lachlan Carrigan, a native of Melbourne, Australia, has emerged as one of the top punters in college football this season, earning a spot on the Ray Guy Award Midseason Watch List announced Thursday. Carrigan, who grew up in Melbourne before making his way to Southern California, has become a valuable weapon for the Trojans with his ability to flip field position and pin opponents deep in their own territory. The Ray Guy Award, named after the legendary NFL punter and Pro Football Hall of Famer, is presented annually to the nation's top collegiate punter in the Football Bowl Subdivision. Carrigan is averaging an impressive 48.7 yards on 17 punts this season, a mark that would rank fifth nationally among qualifying punters. However, he does not meet the NCAA leaderboard's minimum requirement of 3.6 punts per game, largely because USC's offense has limited his opportunities. Despite the relatively small number of punts, Carrigan has made the most of his chances. Eight of his 17 punts have traveled at least 50 yards, while six have been downed inside the opponent's 20-yard line. Five have landed at or inside the 10-yard line, including three at or inside the 5. One of his most impressive kicks came against Washington, when he pinned the Huskies at their own 1-yard line, giving USC's defense an opportunity to capitalize on favorable field position. Carrigan has averaged at least 50 yards per punt in three games this season, including a season-best 56.0 yards against Rutgers. He also averaged 52.5 yards against Penn State and 50.0 yards against Louisiana. His combination of distance, accuracy and consistency has made him an important part of USC's special teams unit as the Trojans continue their push toward the College Football Playoff. In addition to his punting responsibilities, Carrigan serves as USC's holder on field goals and extra-point attempts, giving him another important role in the Trojans' kicking game. The Melbourne native is among a growing number of Australian athletes making an impact in American college football, particularly at the punter position. Australia's Australian rules football tradition has helped produce numerous successful college and NFL punters, with players often bringing powerful kicking legs and experience handling the football under pressure. Carrigan's inclusion on the Ray Guy Award watch list puts him in contention for one of college football's most prestigious individual honors for specialists. Candidates were evaluated based on their overall statistics, with particular emphasis on net punting average, percentage of punts placed inside the 20-yard line and percentage of punts that were not returned. The Ray Guy Award Committee will select 10 semifinalists, who will be announced Nov. 13. From there, a national voting body consisting of FBS sports information directors, media representatives and previous Ray Guy Award winners will select three finalists. The winner will be announced Dec. 11

item.title: Sharks Insight: Does San Jose Need Different Voice Besides Warsofsky?
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Have the San Jose Sharks checked out on Ryan Warsofsky? Last Saturday, in a flatfooted 5-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators, it looked like yes. On Monday, in a genuinely well-played 2-1 loss to the Calgary Flames, it looked like no. On Wednesday, in an inexplicable 7-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings, it looked like yes. But either way, the San Jose Sharks need to respond on Friday and Saturday, in a tough back-to-back against Stanley Cup contenders, the Minnesota Wild and Dallas Stars. And it’s fair to judge Warsofsky’s future on how they respond. It’s not to say that the Sharks need to peel off a 10-game winning streak. The loss to Los Angeles does mean San Jose has dropped five of their last six. But San Jose needs to play hard and connected, two things that an NHL team should be able to accomplish, and which they failed to do against Los Angeles. The team held a players-only meeting after the blowout at Crypto.com Arena. Afterwards, Kiefer Sherwood , perhaps aware of the talk hanging around Warsofsky, said unprompted, “It’s not on the coaches right now.” Captain Macklin Celebrini pointed out the obvious, “We’re the ones on the ice.” Disconnected goals like Adrian Kempe ’s first two and Erik Haula ’s stroll down the slot are not, in my opinion, coaching mistakes. That’s just bad hockey from a team that’s too in its head. But of course, it is on the coaching staff to help guide the team out of their mental shadows. Look, it’s a game of mistakes. Kempe gets breakaway goal 1:23 in. No big deal, you’re just down a goal. It’s how you respond to mistakes. “We’re not winning our battles. We’re not being hard to play against. We’re not making plays,” Sherwood said. Per Stathletes, the Kings had four high-danger chances at 5-on-5, the Sharks zero. That tracks. Stathletes, by the way, has a much different measure for high-danger chances than public models: They’re shot attempts with a higher than 20 percent Expected Goals each. item.title: Kevin Durant feels attacked by internet ‘minions’
item.description: Screengrab from Ballislife on X Kevin Durant has no problem calling out a reporter, but he doesn’t like seeing anyone call him out on social media. Earlier this week, Durant got testy with a reporter for asking about his offensive impact this season with the Houston Rockets. After attempting just six shots in their win over the Boston Celtics Monday night, Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle tried to ask about balancing Durant’s ability to open the offense for his teammates with being aggressive. But Durant kept interrupting Shankar, accusing him of being critical. “Why does that matter to you?” Durant asked before letting Shankar finish his question. “We won the game. Why are you singling me out?” After he interjected several times, Durant eventually heard the full question and offered a thoughtful answer. But the back-and-forth would ultimately go viral. And following Houston’s loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves Wednesday night, Durant opened his postgame press conference by asking Shankar to tell everyone online to back off. Kevin Durant “It’s all love in here. It’s supposed to be a family atmosphere, right? We go back and forth. Can we not? Make sure your minions online know that. I got attacked. item.title: “We can change the game whenever”: Kobbie Mainoo’s words will strike fear into Aston Villa hearts
item.description: “We can change the game whenever”: Kobbie Mainoo’s words will strike fear into Aston Villa hearts After almost no wins in two months, Manchester United produced another comeback for the ages as they beat AS Roma 3-2 in the Champions League. The win will do the squad a world of good, considering the pressure they have been under, and it will also ease the scrutiny on Michael Carrick. However, the victory will not mean much if the Red Devils cannot carry that momentum into their all-important Premier League clash against Aston Villa on Sunday. Kobbie Mainoo was asked by Amazon Prime about the tactical changes that revitalised the 20-time English league champions against the Serie A giants. Carrick’s new bold approach The Carrington graduate explained the head coach’s demands and sent a timely reminder to the Villans about United’s threat moving forward. “The boss really drilled it into us that we needed to be more active and, you know, go and take the game ourselves. We know what we’re capable of. We know we’re a dangerous team and we know we can change the game whenever. It’s just about everything coming together at the right time. Hopefully, we’ll carry that on for the rest of the season.” Interestingly, the mood within the group has changed considerably, with the players hellbent on delivering on the pitch for the club’s fans who have stuck by the team through thick and thin. Kobbie Mainoo vows to do it for the fans “Everyone’s buzzing, you know, and obviously there’s a big sigh of relief. Now we just need to carry on. You know, we’d do anything for these fans on that pitch. All the love that they give us throughout the season, it’s only right that we repay them.” Another special night at Old Trafford awaits. The stadium can do magic, as the Giallorossi found out to their detriment. The West Midlands team could also be in for a rude shock, provided Carrick gets his tactics and selection spot on, as he also knows what works and what does not . United will also come face-to-face with Unai Emery, the manager tipped to be Carrick’s ideal successor . However, Villa are close to agreeing a new long-term deal with the Spaniard. Instead, the new world champion chose to clinch the title with a late-braking lunge on Charles Leclerc into Turn 1, and not everyone at Mercedes was comfortable watching it. Speaking on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show , Antonelli revealed that some members of the team questioned why he had taken the risk, with the championship already within touching distance. "Couldn't you have just stayed behind?" Host Anthony Davidson said the move had left the team "holding their breath", describing it as "necessary but not necessary at the same time". "Some of them, they were like, 'Couldn't you have just stayed behind?'" Antonelli laughed. "But of course, I wanted to finish on the podium. I wanted to clinch the title with a good race. I didn't want to just clinch it by doing the normal job, which was OK, finish ninth." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Antonelli believes he had more than a podium in him before the race was stopped. Running an offset strategy in the first stint, he said he was set up for a strong second half of the race on much fresher tyres. "I really believe that after the pitstop we could have even fought for maybe a win, because the pace was very strong and the car was feeling great," he said. The red flag reset the field, leaving him fourth for the restart with everyone on fresh tyres. Antonelli said he saw it as a chance, and took third place from Leclerc to finish behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton . The risk did not end there, either. Mercedes has since revealed that Antonelli was close to retiring with an oil leak in the closing laps. Lessons from a difficult rookie year That willingness to attack, even with the title on the line, is a far cry from the driver who struggled through spells of his rookie season in 2025. "I'm not going to lie, I've been questioning myself over and over again last season during that stretch," Antonelli admitted on the same show. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes He said being put straight into a Mercedes made it harder, because he was "much more under the spotlight", but credited those difficult moments, including a bad home race at Monza last year, with speeding up his development. "Looking back, I'm very glad that I went through all that difficult moments, because I think they shaped me. They made me grow a lot faster. They made me mature a lot faster," the 20-year-old said.
